questions.topic: Marrow · 65.Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
questions.stem: Which of the following is more likely to be susceptible to alkylation with a bifunctional alkylating agent?
questions.solutionHtml:
The N7 atom of guanine is particularly susceptible to alkylation with bifunctional alkylating agents. It leads to the formation of a covalent bond with bifunctional alkylating agents and represents the key target in nucleic acids for alkylating agents. Alkylation results in cross-linking/abnormal base pairing of DNA which inhibits DNA replication.

Other sites that can be involved are:

  • N1 and N3 of adenosine 
  • N3 of cytosine 
  • O6 of guanine 




Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no 1169

questions.topic: Marrow · 65.Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
questions.stem: During a study on the cytotoxic effects of alkylating agents, you observe that cyclophosphamide has a higher cytotoxic effect compared to procarbazine. Which property of cyclophosphamide is the reason for this?
questions.solutionHtml:
Cyclophosphamide (nitrogen mustard) is a bifunctional alkylating agent and it results in cross-linking of DNA that causes a major disruption in nucleic acid function and increased cytotoxicity. 

Procarbazine is a monofunctional alkylating agent.

Differences between bifunctional and monofunctional alkylating agents are:

Bifunctional alkylating agents

 Monofunctional alkylating  agents
Usually transfers ethyl group to DNA resulting in cross-linking Usually transfers a methyl group resulting in simple methylation. No cross-linking of DNA

Higher cytotoxicity because of cross-linking results in a greater threat to cellular survival

Higher carcinogenesis risk as simple methylation can be bypassed by DNA polymerases resulting in permanent modification of DNA sequence




Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no 1171

questions.topic: Marrow · 65.Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
questions.stem: Which among the following is not an alkylating agent?
questions.solutionHtml:
5-Flourouracil is a pyrimidine analogue and is an antimetabolite.





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page nos 1169-1175

questions.topic: Marrow · 65.Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
questions.stem: Which of the following is not a nitrogen mustard?
questions.solutionHtml:
Carmustine belongs to the nitrosourea class of alkylating agents. 





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page nos 1169 and 1174

questions.topic: Marrow · 65.Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
questions.stem: Temozolomide is used as a first-line agent for the management of which of the following conditions?
questions.solutionHtml:
Temozolomide is used as a first-line agent for the management of glioblastoma multiforme. It is used for newly diagnosed cases along with radiotherapy and also used for maintenance therapy.

Temozolomide belongs to the triazene group of alkylating agents and is administered orally. The oral bioavailability of temozolomide is nearly 100%.

In anaplastic astrocytoma, refractory cases with disease progression are treated with a regimen containing nitrosourea and procarbazine.





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no. 1175
Online Resource, https://www.cancernetwork.com/view/role-temozolomide-cns

questions.topic: Marrow · 65.Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
questions.stem: A patient is diagnosed with astrocytoma. Which of the following drugs crosses the blood brain barrier and hence can be used for the treatment of this condition?
questions.solutionHtml:
Lomustine can cross the blood-brain barrier and is used in the management of brain tumours like astrocytoma.

Nitrosoureas like lomustine and carmustine are highly lipophilic drugs and can easily cross the blood-brain barrier. Hence, they are indicated in the management of brain tumors.





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no 1174

questions.topic: Marrow · 65.Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
questions.stem: Which of the following drugs is not an anthracycline antibiotic?
questions.solutionHtml:
Dactinomycin or actinomycin D is an actinomycin and not an anthracycline antibiotic.





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no 1190

questions.topic: Marrow · 65.Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
questions.stem: Topical mitomycin C is used in which of the following patients?

options.label: C
options.text: A patient undergoing endoscopic treatment of angiofibroma

questions.solutionHtml:
Topical mitomycin C is used in laryngotracheal stenosis.

Mitomycin C is an antitumor antibiotic that inhibits cell division, protein synthesis and fibroblast proliferation. Topical mitomycin C has been shown to cause symptomatic improvement when applied to patients with laryngotracheal stenosis.





Prescribing Information, Rahbar R, Shapshay SM, Healy GB. Mitomycin: effects on laryngeal and tracheal stenosis, benefits, and complications. Ann Otol Rhinol Laryngol. 2001 Jan;110(1):1-6
Cummings Otolaryngology: Head and Neck Surgery 17th edition, Page no. 180, 955, 3115

questions.topic: Marrow · 65.Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
questions.stem: A patient with superficial bladder carcinoma is being treated with a drug by intravesical therapy. Identify this drug.
questions.solutionHtml:
Mitomycin C is used in the treatment of superficial transitional cell carcinoma by intravesical instillation. It is also used in upper gastrointestinal cancers (e.g. esophageal carcinoma), anal cancers, and breast cancers.

Topical mitomycin C is used in:

  • Superficial bladder cancer
  • Intraperitoneal tumors
  • Strabismus surgery to reduce scarring
  • To prevent tracheal and esophageal stenosis
  • Post nasal surgery synechae formation




Tripathi's Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology 7th Edition, Page no 868
Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no 1193

questions.topic: Marrow · 65.Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
questions.stem: A patient was diagnosed with acute promyelocytic leukemia and chemotherapy was initiated. The patient achieved complete remission. However, after a few months molecular relapse was detected. Which of the following drugs would be highly effective in this case?
questions.solutionHtml:
Arsenic trioxide (ATO) is highly effective in relapsed or refractory acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL). It acts by enhancing reactive oxygen free radical generation in APL cells.

Tretinoin and idarubicin (anthracycline) are usually first-line agents for acute promyelocytic leukemia.





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no 1196

questions.topic: Marrow · 65.Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
questions.stem: A patient with osteosarcoma was initiated on chemotherapy. After a few days, he developed dysuria and hematuria. Which group of drugs among the following is most likely to have caused this complication?
questions.solutionHtml:
This scenario depicts haemorrhagic cystitis and the possible cause could be alkylating agents like ifosfamide. 

Chemotherapeutic agents used for the treatment of osteosarcoma include ifosfamide, which is one of the commonest drugs causing haemorrhagic cystitis.

Ifosfamide is a nitrogen mustard and belongs to the alkylating agents. 





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no 1173
Online Resource, https://www.uptodate.com/contents/chemotherapy-and-radiation-related-hemorrhagic-cystitis-in-cancer-patients

questions.topic: Marrow · 65.Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
questions.stem: Hemorrhagic cystitis is a characteristic side effect of which of the following drugs?
questions.solutionHtml:
Hemorrhagic cystitis is a characteristic side effect of cyclophosphamide. The metabolite responsible for hemorrhagic cystitis is acrolein. This can be decreased by vigorous hydration and by the use of mercapto ethane sulfonic acid (mesna).





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no 1173

questions.topic: Marrow · 65.Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
questions.stem: A 62-year-old woman with breast carcinoma is started on cyclophosphamide. What is the rationale behind using sodium 2-mercaptoethanesulfonate along with this drug?
questions.solutionHtml:
Sodium 2-mercaptoethanesulfonate (MESNA) is given along with cyclophosphamide to reduce the incidence of hemorrhagic cystitis.    

MESNA concentrates in the bladder where acrolein accumulates after administration of cyclophosphamide and ifosfamide. It forms a conjugate with acrolein and other urotoxic metabolites. This conjugation reaction inactivates the urotoxic compounds to harmless metabolites which are excreted in the urine.





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no: 1172,1173

questions.topic: Marrow · 65.Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
questions.stem: Which of the following statements about ifosfamide is false?

options.label: C
options.text: Chloroacetaldehyde is the metabolite of ifosfamide

questions.solutionHtml:
Ifosfamide is more neurotoxic than cyclophosphamide. It causes greater platelet suppression, nephrotoxicity, and urothelial damage when compared to cyclophosphamide.

Ifosfamide is a nitrogen mustard (alkylating agent). It is metabolized by hydroxylation by cytochrome P450 enzymes. Chloroacetaldehyde is a metabolite of ifosfamide that is responsible for severe neurological adverse effects.





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, page no 1172

questions.topic: Marrow · 65.Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
questions.stem: A 67 year old woman with a malignant lump in the breast who is undergoing chemotherapy, presents with shortness of breath, tachycardia and hypertension. ECG shows ST and T wave changes. Which among the following drugs could have led to this?
questions.solutionHtml:
This scenario depicts Doxorubicin induced cardiotoxicity. It is a unique adverse effect of doxorubicin. It is an anthracycline group of anticancer antibiotics.

Doxorubicin-induced cardiomyopathy takes two forms:

  • Acute: pericarditis-myocarditis syndrome, arrhythmias, ST and T wave changes in ECG.
  • Chronic: dilated cardiomyopathy.

Note: Dexrazoxane is a cardioprotective iron-chelating agent that is indicated for use along with high dose doxorubicin to avoid cardiotoxicity.





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page nos 1191 and 1192

questions.topic: Marrow · 65.Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
questions.stem: A 54-year-old man is diagnosed with Kaposi sarcoma. You are planning to start chemotherapy with doxorubicin, which can cause cardiotoxicity. Which of the following drugs would you prescribe to prevent this?
questions.solutionHtml:
Dexrazoxane is a cardioprotective iron-chelating agent that is indicated for use along with high dose doxorubicin to avoid cardiotoxicity. The exact cardioprotective mechanism of dexrazoxane is unknown and it appears not to compromise with anticancer activity of doxorubicin.





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no 1192

questions.topic: Marrow · 65.Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
questions.stem: Least cardiotoxicity is seen with which of the following anthracycline antibiotic?
questions.solutionHtml:
Idarubicin has least cardiotoxicity when compared to other anthracyclines.

It is approved for use in acute myeloid leukemia along with cytarabine. Doxorubicin, daunorubicin and epirubicin share similar cardiotoxicity profile.





Online Resource, https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/10507317

questions.topic: Marrow · 65.Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
questions.stem: While reviewing the drug chart of a patient undergoing radiotherapy, which of the following drugs would require a dose adjustment to prevent radiation toxicity?
questions.solutionHtml:
Doxorubicin requires dose adjustment during or after radiotherapy in order to prevent radiation toxicity.

Anthracyclines like doxorubicin can result in a radiation recall reaction, where erythema and desquamation of skin are observed at sites of previous radiation injury. The risk of cardiotoxicity also increases with previous irradiation. Therefore, careful monitoring and dosage adjustments are required for doxorubicin.





Katzung's Basic and Clinical Pharmacology 12/E (Lange Basic Science), Page no 966
Katzung Basic and Clinical Pharmacology - 14th Edition, Page no 965

questions.topic: Marrow · 65.Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
questions.stem: A patient is undergoing chemotherapy for glioblastoma multiforme. You notice that his serial blood investigations reveal sustained neutropenia. Which of the following drugs could have caused this?
questions.solutionHtml:
Sustained neutropenia is seen with nitrosoureas. Nitrosoureas like carmustine and lomustine cause profound and delayed myelosuppression with recovery 4-6 weeks after a single dose.





Online Resource, https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC5132417/
Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no: 1174,1175

questions.topic: Marrow · 65.Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
questions.stem: A patient with Hodgkin’s disease on chemotherapy with an alkylating agent develops behavioral disturbances and experiences sedation. He presented to the emergency room with a disulfiram-like reaction. What is the drug being described here?
questions.solutionHtml:
The most likely alkylating agent being described here is procarbazine. It is associated with behavioural disturbances and sedation. Concomitant CNS depressants should be avoided.

Procarbazine is a weak MAO inhibitor and can potentiate tyramine and catecholamines action. It also has disulfiram-like actions and alcohol should be avoided. 





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 14th Edition, Page no; 1351

questions.topic: Marrow · 65.Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
questions.stem: A 50 year old man who presented with dysphagia was diagnosed with esophageal carcinoma and underwent multiple cycles of chemotherapy. During the cycles, he had developed tingling and numbness in the lower limbs and the symptoms progressed even after cessation of the cycles. Which drug could have led to this?
questions.solutionHtml:
The scenario depicts coasting effect neuropathy, which is seen with cisplatin.

The coasting effect means the progression of symptoms even after the cessation of the drug. Neurotoxicity is usually dependent on the cumulative dose of anticancer drugs. The severity of neuropathy increases with the duration of treatment and progression stops once drug treatment is completed. 

Platinum compounds are an exception, where sensory loss progresses for several months after cessation of treatment. The coasting effect is more common with cisplatin and oxaliplatin than with carboplatin.





Journal, Grisold W, Cavaletti G, Windebank AJ. Peripheral neuropathies from chemotherapeutics and targeted agents: diagnosis, treatment, and prevention. Neuro-Oncology. 2012;14(Suppl 4):iv45-iv54. doi:10.1093/neuonc/nos203.]
Online Resource, https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC5554876/

questions.topic: Marrow · 65.Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
questions.stem: A 65 year old man who was diagnosed with small cell carcinoma of the lung had undergone chemotherapy about 5 years ago. Now he presents with features suggestive of AML. Which of the following drugs could have caused this condition?
questions.solutionHtml:
The scenario is suggestive of secondary leukemia which is associated with cisplatin. Cisplatin is a platinum-containing anticancer agent that forms DNA adduct. It is associated with the development of AML usually more than 4 years after treatment.

Procarbazine, a methylhydralazine (alkylating agent), is most commonly associated with the development of leukemias with a 5-10% risk of acute leukemia in patients treated with the MOPP regimen.

Cisplatin produces responses in cancers of the bladder, head and neck, cervix, and endometrium; all forms of carcinoma of the lung; anal and rectal carcinomas; and neoplasms of childhood.





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page nos. 1176 and 1177

questions.topic: Marrow · 65.Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
questions.stem: A patient who was diagnosed with gastric carcinoma is undergoing chemotherapy. His serum creatinine levels are rising and you suspect renal tubular damage caused by one of his chemotherapeutic drugs. Which drug could it be?
questions.solutionHtml:
The given scenario is suggesstive of nephrotoxicity and it is one of the dose-limiting toxicity of cisplatin therapy. Cisplatin achieves a high concentration in nephrons. Both direct toxicity and inflammation are responsible for nephrotoxicity. A high concentration of chloride stabilizes cisplatin and reduces nephrotoxicity. Therefore, chloride diuresis is used to reduce nephrotoxicity.

Option B - Streptozotocin use can result in diabetes mellitus due to the destruction of beta cells of the pancreas.

Option C - Methysergide use is associated with retroperitoneal fibrosis.

Option D - Cyclophosphamide causes hemorrhagic cystitis as one of its characteristic side effect.





Katzung's Basic and Clinical Pharmacology 12/E (Lange Basic Science), Page no 956
Prescribing Information, Miller RP, Tadagavadi RK, Ramesh G, Reeves WB. Mechanisms of Cisplatin Nephrotoxicity. Toxins. 2010;2(11):2490-2518. doi:10.3390/toxins2112490

questions.topic: Marrow · 65.Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
questions.stem: Which among the following is a highly emetogenic anticancer drug?
questions.solutionHtml:
Cisplatin is a highly emetogenic anticancer drug. Cisplatin causes marked nausea and vomiting in almost all cases and is usually administered along with anti-emetic regimens.

This can usually be controlled with 5HT3 receptor antagonists, neurokinin (NK1) receptor antagonists (e.g., aprepitant), and high-dose corticosteroids.





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no: 1176

questions.topic: Marrow · 65.Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
questions.stem: A patient who is undergoing chemotherapy for testicular cancer, now presents with dyspnea and dry cough. Investigations suggest pulmonary fibrosis. This condition is commonly associated with which of the following drugs?
questions.solutionHtml:
Pulmonary fibrosis is commonly seen with bleomycin. The main abnormality in bleomycin toxicity occurs in endothelial and epithelial cells. This leads to the destruction and desquamation of type I pneumocytes and the resultant hyperplasia of type II pneumocytes. 

Pulmonary toxicity begins with a dry cough, fine rales, and diffuse basal infiltrates on X-ray and may progress to life-threatening pulmonary fibrosis. No specific treatment is available to ameliorate the toxicity and managed by general symptomatic care.



Note: Few case reports of methotrexate causing pulmonary fibrosis are reported. The association is still uncertain as the underlying disease process like RA can also contribute to fibrosis. 





Online Resource, https://www.mdedge.com/rheumatologynews/article/165649/rheumatoid-arthritis/methotrexate-induced-pulmonary-fibrosis-risk
Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no 1193

questions.topic: Marrow · 65.Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
questions.stem: A patient who is undergoing chemotherapy, now presents with weight gain, ascites, hepatomegaly and hyperbilirubinemia. You suspect sinusoidal obstruction syndrome. Which drug is the most common cause of this condition?
questions.solutionHtml:
Sinusoidal obstruction syndrome is most commonly associated with high-dose busulfan. Incidence increases when coadministered with CYP inhibitors.

Sinusoidal obstruction syndrome, previously known as veno-occlusive hepatic disease (VOD), involves primary hepatic sinusoidal injury that progresses to diffuse hepatocyte involvement and panvasculitis. This leads to multi-organ failure, and can be life-threatening.





Online Resource, https://www.uptodate.com/contents/diagnosis-of-hepatic-sinusoidal-obstruction-syndrome-veno-occlusive-disease-following-hematopoietic-cell-transplantation#H1
Online Resource, https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC3872829/
Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no: 1174

questions.topic: Marrow · 65.Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
questions.stem: A patient undergoing chemotherapy was brought to the ER with seizures. He is diagnosed with cerebrovascular accident which you suspect to be due to a drug-induced hypercoagulable state. Which of the following drugs is implicated?
questions.solutionHtml:
L-asparaginase causes a hypercoagulable state. It is an enzyme and toxicity results due to the inhibition of protein synthesis in normal tissues.

Side effects of L-asparaginase:

  • Thrombosis and increased coagulation - physiological anticlotting factors are impaired
  • Hemorrhage and bleeding - clotting factors are impaired
  • Hyperglycemia - insulin deficiency.




Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no 1195

questions.topic: Marrow · 65.Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
questions.stem: Which of the following drugs causes flagellate pigmentation?
questions.solutionHtml:
Flagellate hyperpigmentation/flagellate erythema is a characteristic cutaneous reaction to treatment with bleomycin. 

Clinical features include multiple linear streaks (erythematous or hyperpigmented) at sites of trauma and generalized pruritus.






Online Resource, https://www.uptodate.com/contents/acquired-hyperpigmentation-disorders#
Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Pg 1284

questions.topic: Marrow · 65.Non Cell Cycle Specific Cytotoxic Drugs
questions.stem: Which of the following drugs cause carcinoma bladder?
questions.solutionHtml:
The only chemotherapeutic agent that has been proven to cause bladder cancer is cyclophosphamide.

The risk of the bladder cancer formation is linearly related to the duration and intensity of cyclophosphamide treatment, supporting a causative role. Phosphoramide mustard is the primary mutagenic metabolite that causes bladder cancer in patients exposed to cyclophosphamide.





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page nos 1172 and 1173
Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery - 27th Edition, Page no 1446
